subject.title: [Feature]: Allow job-level model override for cron jobs using sessionTarget=main + payload.kind=systemEvent

question: Should main-session systemEvent cron jobs support a first-class model/provider override, and which single public API shape should own it?
rationale: The request changes public cron protocol plus provider/session routing semantics, so automation should not choose between `payload.model`, top-level job fields, or a `sessionOverride` block without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add one canonical job-level override
options.body: Define one job-level override contract, validate it through current model allowlist/fallback logic, and pass it to main-session heartbeat execution without encoding routing state into event text.

options.title: Reuse payload.model on systemEvent
options.body: Extend the existing payload field as the smallest schema change, accepting that text-only system events would also carry run-routing metadata.

options.title: Keep main systemEvent default-only
options.body: Document that per-cron cheap models require isolated or custom agent-turn jobs and leave main-session system events on their session/default model.

recommendation.title: Add one canonical job-level override
recommendation.body: Define one job-level override contract, validate it through current model allowlist/fallback logic, and pass it to main-session heartbeat execution without encoding routing state into event text.

likelyOwner.reason: The current cron protocol, type, validation, and main execution lines blame to Vincent Koc's recent PR, making him the best available code-path owner for the API decision.
